critique: The lower-frame water-impact zone is present, but it currently reads as a small cloud of bright particle dots rather than clean expanding ripple rings. The two frames do not provide a clear readable ring expansion. More importantly, there are no visible falling rain drops or streaks anywhere above the water zone, so the intended drop-to-impact causality is absent. The ripple source is centered while the rain emitter is extremely wide, which would also weaken the landing connection once rain becomes visible.

suggestions.why: Slow the falling particles enough that individual drops remain visibly readable in-frame instead of becoming extremely faint fast motion-blur traces.
With the reduced downward velocity, end drop life near the y~560 waterline so drops visually terminate at the ripple zone.
Make the falling rain particles bright and legible against the very dark background.
Concentrate rainfall around the existing central ripple source so visible drops can plausibly land where rings form.
Keep approximately 100 ripple particles per impact but emit them in a much shorter burst, producing a thinner, more readable expanding ring rather than a filled dot cloud.
Keep the linked live particle-rate control synchronized with the shorter ring-generation burst.
